chapter: Central Avenue, WPA and the Alabam era
title: The WPA and free concerts
summary: Blakeney did not take part in the WPA but remembers WPA band concerts at the union hall.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: During the mid thirties, after the election of President Franklin D. Roosevelt, there was a major social program, in addition to the social security program, called the WPA, or the Work Project Administration, and this program effected many musicians; can you tell me what you remember about the WPA, Mr. Blakeney?
There's not much I can remember about the WPA, I didn't participate in the WPA too much because--I don't know.
Where were some of the concerts held? Were there concerts held by the WPA bands?
Yes, I remember a concert at the union hall at meetings.
Did the people in the community come out to these free concerts?

The WPA also touched other artists, not just musicians. There were singers all involved in the WPA program; it was geared to the low income persons at that time who was out of work, so I would think that many of the black musicians probably participated; is that right?
Yes; that's the way I see it, yes.
